title: Scheduler-induced attention shard tearing causing state-cache incoherence and subtle numeric drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During recent scheduler changes to support concurrent attention shard execution across multiple kernels, we observed rare correctness regressions in long-context decoding workloads. Symptoms include off-by-one token shifts in generated text, low-frequency numeric drift in softmax outputs for later timesteps, and occasional mismatch between cached key/value state and live kernel state leading to token hallucination in edge cases.
observed_behavior: 1) For some long sequences (>2048 tokens) under heavy throughput, a subset of requests produce deterministic but incorrect continuations (token alignment shifted by 1-3 positions). 2) In traces captured with extended FP32 logging, softmax probabilities in later decode steps show slight drift versus baseline (up to 1e-3 differences) that accumulates. 3) In a small fraction (~0.1%) of requests during concurrent shard swaps, the K/V buffer appears to be read from an earlier slot (stale pointers) resulting in coherent but wrong context.
environment: Repro on internal canary cluster with runtime-1.20 branch including scheduler v3.4. Tests run on A100 and RTX8000; more frequent on high-concurrency A100 pools. Repro rate increases when batch sizes are high and using quantized kernels + mixed-precision fallback.
steps_taken: 1) Added deterministic trace mode and granular sequence-number tagging across scheduler -> kernel RPC boundaries. 2) Instrumented KV slab headers and pointer stamping (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123). 3) Replayed failing traces with single-threaded scheduler to isolate concurrency dependence. 4) Ran numeric diff harness against golden baseline for softmax and attention scores.
findings: - Root cause appears to be a race in the scheduler's shard handoff path: when a concurrent prefill finishes while decode workers are rebalancing shards, a stale slab pointer can be returned to the decode path before the pointer's generation counter increments. This leads to reading a K/V region owned by a previous request. - A secondary issue: kernel selection logic sometimes returns an optimized fused-attention kernel that assumes contiguous per-shard offsets; during a mid-epoch shard rotation the kernel receives offsets computed against a different mapping, producing subtle index misreads and floating-point accumulation differences. - The numeric drift is small per-step but amplifies across long horizons because the wrong K/V causes slightly different attention weights which change subsequent cached writes (feedback loop).
impact_analysis: Scope: affects long-context decoding when shard rotation/rebalancing happens concurrently with prefill -> decode boundary. Customer visible rate estimated at <0.5% for typical workloads, higher for heavy multi-tenant A100 pools using aggressive shard reallocation. Risks: content integrity regressions and potential downstream eval failures for regression suites. Not believed to be data-exfiltration or security-sensitive.
proposed_fix: 1) Add atomic generation stamping to KV slab handles and verify generation on every read path; reject reads if generation mismatches and trigger safe fallback to re-prefill. 2) Harden scheduler handoff by introducing a short quiesce window when rotating shard ownership (configurable, default 4ms). 3) Tighten kernel-selection compatibility rules: ensure kernel accepts offset-mapping metadata and reject fused kernels if mapping epoch != kernel epoch. 4) Add unit/regression tests that simulate shard rotations mid-prefill and a canary job to run regression traces post-deploy.
rollback_mitigation: If rollout shows higher-than-expected regressions, disable aggressive shard rebalancing (config flag scheduler.enable_hot_reassign=false) and pin affected customers to older runtime-1.19 routing. Emergency patch: enforce single-threaded decode worker for pinned shards until fix lands.
acceptance_criteria: - Zero reproducible token-reordering cases in the regression harness for 10K synthetic long-context traces. - Numeric softmax diffs between baseline and patched runtime within 1e-6 across 2048-token sequences. - No increase in median latency >2% and no regression in throughput SLA for dedicated pools. - New tests in CI and a canary window (72h) on internal canary cluster with telemetry showing <0.05% anomaly rate.
next_steps: 1) Diego to land PR for slab generation stamping and unit tests (blocking). 2) Schedule short quiesce window experiment and measure latency impact (Mon). 3) PM (Lucille Wong) to notify a small set of affected customers under NDA and propose temporary pinning. 4) Add kernel epoch metadata to kernel selection API and update kernel adapters.
